text.p: Agri-Nutrition Group, which reported a narrower loss for the fiscal first quarter ended January 31, said Wednesday it expects improved profitability in fiscal 1997.
"With the focus on developing our core businesses, we continue to expect the combination of our initiatives to result in improved profitability in 1997," Bruce Baker, president, said in a statement.
Income from operations for the first quarter was $87,000 compared with a loss from operations of $228,000. Net loss for the quarter was $30,000 compared with a net loss of $176,000 a year ago.

Net sales were $10.2 million, up 22 percent from year-ago sales of $8.3 million. Higher margin specialty product sales increased by 28 percent to $7.4 million for the first quarter versus $5.8 million in the same quarter of last year.

"We are pleased with the improvement in sales and gross profit as well as our ability to generate income from operations versus a loss last year," Baker said. "Also, our reduction in corporate costs is having a positive impact."
Agri-Nutrition Group operates three companies that produce, market and distribute health, grooming, and nutritional products for the pet and animal health care industry.
